nina: Thinking out loudwhat if we move sampling controls into the time-range picker instead of the heatmap header? keeps heatmap cleaner on mobile. sketch: https://redwood.internal/figma/timepicker-sampler (quick). omar: Hmm I like reducing chrome. But two concerns: discoverability and whether users associate sampling with time-range. ting: a11y first: if its inside a composite control make sure the timepicker has a clear tab order and that sampling is reachable via arrow keys. Also announce state changes. paul: Copy thought: label the control "Data sampling" and sublabel "percent of requests shown" so users don't confuse with timespan sampling. robotux: small mock uploaded: timepicker-sample-inline.png :frame_with_picture: https://redwood.design/timepicker-sample-inline.png rachel: UX idea: show a subtle pill inside the timepicker "Sample: 10%". Tapping opens a mini-popover with presets + short explanation "Lower sampling reduces visual noise but may hide spikes". omar: Also add a p95 tooltip hint when sampling < 100% show a small badge on the p95 metric card "based on sampled data" (hover explains confidence). paul: Nice, we should avoid alarmist copy. Suggest: "p95 (estimated from sample)" and a tooltip: "Estimated from a sample of requests; lower sampling increases uncertainty." Keep language light. ting: Accessibility nits: avoid relying on color for the badge. Use an icon + short text. For colorblind users use diagonal hatch pattern on heatmap legend for sampled vs full. rachel: Also run a micro-usability test: 5 users, mobile & desktop, see if they find sampling in timepicker. If >20% fail to find it, fallback to header pill. paul: Implementation constraints: timepicker is already a complex component with ARIA roles. Adding a popover is fine if we keep it outside the canvas and trap focus while open. Devs: can we keep popover DOM sibling to timepicker? devbot: technical note: current timepicker uses a dropdown portal at body level. Popover for sampling can reuse that portal and the existing focus-trap util. nina: Metrics: product wants to track discovery. Add telemetry events: ui.sampling.open_from="timepicker" or "header" and ui.sampling.apply. Also track whether user used preset or manual slider. omar: UX tweak: change pill copy options: 'Sampled 10%' vs 'Sample: 10%'. I prefer 'Sample: 10%' for brevity. ting: keyboard example for accessibility team: ```html
...
``` rachel: QA checklist: focus order, Escape closes, Tab cycles inside popover, screenreader announces context and percentage changes via aria-live polite. Test VoiceOver rotor navigation. nina: Decision proposal: prototype timepicker-integrated sampling for the usability pass with telemetry hooks. If discoverability <80% we'll iterate to header pill. Paul, devs, can you prototype a non-blocking A/B? paul: Yes. I'll spin up a lightweight feature-flagged experiment: variant A (timepicker) / B (header pill). Should be doable in a day for front-end stub and telemetry. nina: Great. I'll update figma, add acceptance criteria, and create ticket RDW-UI-1402 with accessibility checklist and telemetry events. Thanks :pray:
